episodes.title: Why Deserts Sit Near Thirty Degrees
sources: NCERT, Fundamentals of Physical Geography (Class XI, 2020-21), ch. 10 and ch. 9 (archive.org ncert-kegy2, read 2026-11-19)

quiz.q: Around which latitudes do the subtropical highs sit?
quiz.why: NCERT: along 30 degrees N and S are found the subtropical highs.

quiz.q: What is the tropical circulation cell called?
quiz.why: NCERT: such a cell in the tropics is called the Hadley cell.

quiz.q: Why do the subtropical deserts receive the most insolation?
options: They are closest to the Sun
quiz.why: NCERT: maximum insolation is received over the subtropical deserts, where cloudiness is the least.

episodes.title: The Godavari, Source to Sea
sources: Central Water Commission / India-WRIS basin figures as summarised there

quiz.q: Where does the Godavari rise?
quiz.why: It rises in the Western Ghats at Trimbakeshwar, Nashik district, Maharashtra.

quiz.q: Which tributary, with the Wardha and Wainganga, drains about a third of the basin?
quiz.why: The Pranahita sub-basin, including the Wardha, Wainganga and Penganga, covers about 34% of the basin.

quiz.q: Into which two main branches does the Godavari split at Rajahmundry?
quiz.why: Below the Dowleswaram Barrage it divides into the Gautami and Vasishta Godavari.

episodes.title: Why Cyclones Favour the Bay of Bengal
sources: NCERT, Fundamentals of Physical Geography (Class XI, 2020-21), ch. 10 'Tropical Cyclones' (archive.org ncert-kegy2, kegy210, read 2026-11-19)
Wikipedia, 'North Indian Ocean tropical cyclone' and 'Storm surge' (read 2026-11-19)

quiz.q: A tropical cyclone needs a large sea surface warmer than about:
quiz.why: NCERT lists sea surface temperature higher than 27°C as a favourable condition.

quiz.q: What is the calm centre of a mature tropical cyclone called?
quiz.why: The eye is a region of calm with subsiding air; the eye wall around it has the strongest winds.

quiz.q: What happens to a cyclone when it reaches land?
options: Its moisture supply is cut off and it dissipates
quiz.why: NCERT: on reaching land the moisture supply is cut off and the storm dissipates.

episodes.title: Why Jamshedpur Is Where It Is
sources: NCERT, India: People and Economy (Class XII, 2020-21), ch. 8 'Manufacturing Industries', iron and steel, TISCO (archive.org ncert-legy2, legy208, read 2026-11-19)

quiz.q: Why are iron and steel plants best placed near their raw materials?
options: The raw materials lose weight in processing
Steel is very light to carry
Ports are always next to mines
quiz.why: NCERT calls iron ore and coking coal gross (weight-losing) materials, so plants sit near them.

quiz.q: Which two rivers give water to the Tata plant at Jamshedpur?
quiz.why: NCERT: the rivers Subarnarekha and Kharkai provide water to the plant. The Barakar serves the IISCO plants.

quiz.q: Which port, about 240 km away, is the nearest for exporting the plant's steel?
quiz.why: NCERT: the plant is about 240 km from Kolkata, the nearest port for export of steel.

episodes.title: Black Soil, Red Soil, Laterite
sources: NCERT, India: Physical Environment (Class XI, 2006 edition, archive.org copy dli.scoerat.1650indiaphysicalenvironment), ch. 6 'Soils' (read 2026-11-19)

quiz.q: Which soil is described as 'self ploughing' because it cracks when dry?
quiz.why: NCERT: black soils swell when wet and shrink and crack when dry, a kind of self ploughing.

quiz.q: 'Laterite' comes from a Latin word meaning what?
quiz.why: NCERT: 'later' means brick; laterite is widely cut as bricks.

quiz.q: Black, red and laterite soils are all poor in which nutrient?
quiz.why: NCERT lists nitrogen among the shortfalls of all three; black soil is rich in lime and potash, and laterite has iron and potash in excess.

episodes.title: Reading India's Earthquake Zone Map
sources: NCERT, India: Physical Environment (Class XI, 2020-21), ch. 7 'Natural Hazards and Disasters' (archive.org ncert-kegy1, kegy107, read 2026-11-19)
Wikipedia, 'Earthquake zones of India' (zones, zone factors, areas; read 2026-11-19)
Drishti IAS, 'Rollback of Seismic Code of 2025' (13 Mar 2026) and understandupsc.com 'Earthquake Zoning in India' (9 Mar 2026), read 2026-11-19

quiz.q: How many zones does the current seismic zoning map of IS 1893 (Part 1) have?
quiz.why: The code in force has four zones, II to V; Zone I is not used.

quiz.q: Which of these lies in Zone V, the very high damage risk zone?
quiz.why: Kutch is listed in Zone V; Bengaluru, Jaipur and Hyderabad are in Zone II.

quiz.q: What is a seismic zone map used for?
options: Predicting the date of the next earthquake
quiz.why: Zones set design shaking levels for buildings; they do not predict earthquakes.

episodes.title: The Day the Assembly First Met
sources: Constituent Assembly Debates, Vol. I, 9 December 1946 (constitutionofindia.net/debates/09-dec-1946/, read 2026-11-19)
Wikipedia, 'Constituent Assembly of India' (attendance of 207, Muslim League's 73 seats and boycott; read 2026-11-19)

quiz.q: Who was the temporary chairman at the first sitting of the Constituent Assembly?
quiz.why: J. B. Kripalani invited Dr Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, to take the chair.

quiz.q: On what date did the Constituent Assembly first meet?
quiz.why: The Debates record the first meeting in Constitution Hall, New Delhi, on Monday 9 December 1946.

quiz.q: Which party, with 73 seats from the 1946 election, stayed away from the Assembly?
quiz.why: The Muslim League won 73 seats and boycotted the Assembly (28 of its members later joined).

episodes.title: Ambedkar's Three Warnings
sources: Constituent Assembly Debates, Vol. XI, 25 November 1949, B. R. Ambedkar's closing speech, paras 11.165.323-325, as digitised at constitutionofindia.net/debates/25-nov-1949/ (read 2026-11-19)

quiz.q: What did Ambedkar call the methods of civil disobedience, non-cooperation and satyagraha where constitutional methods are open?
quiz.why: He said these methods are nothing but the Grammar of Anarchy where constitutional methods are open.

quiz.q: According to the speech, hero-worship in politics is a sure road to:
quiz.why: Bhakti in religion may lead to salvation, but in politics it is 'a sure road to degradation and to eventual dictatorship'.

quiz.q: What must political democracy rest on, in his third warning?
quiz.why: He said political democracy cannot last unless social democracy lies at its base.

episodes.title: Union, State, Concurrent
sources: Constitution of India, Articles 246, 248 and 254, and the Seventh Schedule Lists I, II and III, text as reproduced at constitutionofindia.net (read 2026-11-19)

quiz.q: Which article divides law-making powers between Parliament and the states using the three lists?
quiz.why: Article 246 gives Parliament the Union List, both the Concurrent List, and the states the State List.

quiz.q: Which of these is on the Union List?
quiz.why: Entry 36 of List I is currency; public order, agriculture and land are State List subjects.

quiz.q: On a Concurrent List subject, a state law clashes with a Parliament law. Which generally prevails?
quiz.why: Article 254(1): Parliament's law prevails; the state law is void to the extent of the repugnancy. Clause (2) has an exception for presidential assent.

episodes.title: How a Bill Becomes a Law
sources: Constitution of India, Articles 107-111, text as reproduced at constitutionofindia.net (read 2026-11-19)
PRS Legislative Research, 'How is a law enacted in Parliament?', The PRS Blog, 17 March 2010, prsindia.org/theprsblog/how-is-a-law-enacted-in-parliament (read 2026-11-19)

quiz.q: Which kind of bill may not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha?
quiz.why: Article 109(1): a Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Council of States.

quiz.q: How long does the Rajya Sabha have to return a Money Bill with its recommendations?
quiz.why: Article 109(2): within fourteen days; the Lok Sabha may accept or reject the recommendations.

quiz.q: The President returns an ordinary bill, and both Houses pass it again. What may the President do?
quiz.why: Article 111: if the bill is passed again, the President shall not withhold assent.
